text:
maria: Heads-up — starting a small A/B rollout for model-x-13B in eu-west tomorrow 10:00 UTC. Scoped to `beta` customers only. Quick question: if we hit capacity/latency SLOs, should smart routing fallback to model-x-13B-quant (same family, quantized) or to model-y-7B (different variant)?

aaron: Default smart-routing policy today prefers same-tier variant first (so quantized sibling), then cross-variant fallbacks. But we haven't codified per-tier exceptions — e.g., premium/beta customers might explicitly disallow cross-variant fallback.

sam: Agree with aaron. For beta we probably want to avoid model-y-7B unless explicitly allowed. Two options: (A) block cross-variant fallback for `tier=beta` and queue (or shed) requests; (B) allow cross-variant but tag telemetry heavily and route only <1% traffic.

jess: UX/console question — how will this look to customer? We need clear flags in the rollout UI: "allow_cross_variant_fallback" and "fallback_priority" (quantized first, then other families). Also a visible warning if a fallback would change quality level for that customer.

maria: Good point. We should surface expected quality delta + cost delta in the console for each fallback path. We have the components in Optimize to estimate cost, can we reuse that?

aaron: Yes, Optimize can provide cost delta. Quality delta estimate is trickier but we have eval traces per model variant from the evals infra. We can show a relative score and a confidence band.

sam: From implementation side, I'd propose the routing policy schema addition:
```
routes:
  - name: beta-eu-rollout
    match: {tier: beta, region: eu-west}
    primary: model-x-13b
    fallbacks: [model-x-13b-quant, model-y-7b]
    fallback_policy: {type: "ordered", allow_cross_variant: false, cross_variant_threshold: 0.01}
    exposure: {ab: 0.02, canary: 0.0}
```
This would allow explicit deny for cross-variant fallback plus a soft cross-variant threshold if someone flips it on.

lucy: Quick telemetry ask — can we tag every routed request with `route_id`, `fallback_used`, and `fallback_reason` so we can build a per-tier/region dashboard? We need to know if fallbacks are due to capacity, quota, or explicit policy.

maria: deploy-bot: start canary now?

deploy-bot: Canary started for route `beta-eu-rollout` — exposure=2% (rolling), models in rotation: model-x-13b (primary), model-x-13b-quant (fallback1). No cross-variant fallback allowed per policy.

jess: Nice. Also, please add a red-line in the UI: if a fallback would route premium customers to lower-quality variant, show a modal requiring explicit acknowledgement. That avoids accidental regressions.

aaron: One more internal API debate: should the fallback decision be evaluated at the routing layer (fast, no downstream calls) or delegated to the serving runtime which has better visibility into per-GPU queue length? If runtime decides, easier to react to sudden spikes, but harder to enforce per-tenant policy consistently.

sam: My preference: routing layer makes policy decision, runtime reports back health metrics (queue_len, cooldown) and routing layer uses those signals. We can keep a short-circuit hook for emergency runtime-initiated fallback (e.g., node OOM) but that should be auditable.

maria: Agreed. Action items:
- sam: add schema fields `allow_cross_variant` and `cross_variant_threshold` and wire into routing tests (due EOD).
- lucy: add `route_id` + `fallback_reason` to telemetry and create a basic Grafana panel grouped by tier/region (due tomorrow).
- jess: mock console UX for the new flags and the modal for premium customers (sync by EOD).
- aaron: add docs about runtime short-circuit behavior and an audit log entry for emergency fallbacks (due Fri).

lucy: Also recommend we run a 48-hour canary in us-west and eu-west with `allow_cross_variant: false`, then a separate 24-hour run with `allow_cross_variant: true` at 0.1% exposure to capture quality telemetry.

maria: Sounds good. If nobody objects i'll schedule the runs and update the rollout config. If we see any unexpected cross-variant fallbacks in the logs, we'll roll back. :thumbsup:

aaron: No objections from me.

sam: LGTM.

jess: LGTM

deploy-bot: Canary snapshot: route=beta-eu-rollout, exposure=2%, status=rolling, started_by=maria, ts=1778881234

maria: Thanks team — i'll post the rollout link and dashboards once lucy and jess have their bits in place."
